note.explanation: Greenhouse gases let most incoming short-wave sunlight reach Earth’s surface. The warmed surface gives out long-wave radiation, which these gases absorb. This slows the loss of heat to space and raises Earth’s temperature. For example, more CO₂ in the atmosphere increases heat absorption; melting ice and rising sea levels are possible effects of warming.
examples: Example: burning coal, oil and natural gas adds greenhouse gases to the atmosphere.
Example: melting ice in Antarctica and Greenland adds water to the seas and contributes to rising sea levels.
note.checkAnswer: Greenhouse gases absorb some long-wave radiation from Earth and slow the escape of heat to space.
note.simple: Sunlight warms Earth. Earth gives off heat, but greenhouse gases trap some of that heat, so Earth warms further.
note.checkQuestion: Why does a higher concentration of greenhouse gases increase global warming?
note.title: Global Warming (Greenhouse Effect)
steps: Sunlight passes through greenhouse gases and warms Earth’s surface.
The warmed surface gives out long-wave radiation.
Greenhouse gases absorb much of this radiation, so less heat escapes to space.
The temperature of Earth rises; this is global warming.
note.answer: A higher concentration of greenhouse gases absorbs more thermal radiation, causing a greater increase in global warming.

options: It absorbs some long-wave radiation emitted by Earth.
It blocks all short-wave sunlight from reaching Earth.
It makes Earth stop emitting heat at night.
It removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
mcqs.stem: What is the main way greenhouse gases warm Earth?
rationales: Correct: greenhouse gases absorb some of the long-wave radiation emitted by Earth, slowing heat loss to space.
Incorrect: the section says short-wave radiation from the Sun passes through greenhouse gases to heat Earth’s surface.
Incorrect: Earth’s surface still emits long-wave radiation; greenhouse gases absorb much of it.
Incorrect: plants use some carbon dioxide in photosynthesis, but greenhouse gases do not remove it.

options: Burning coal, oil and natural gas
Digestion in animals
Decay of vegetation matter
All of these
mcqs.stem: Which can contribute to the amount of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere?
rationales: Incorrect: burning these fuels adds greenhouse gases, but it is not the only listed source.
Incorrect: digestion in animals contributes to increased methane, but it is not the only listed source.
Incorrect: increased decay of vegetation matter contributes to methane, but it is not the only listed source.
Correct: burning fossil fuels adds greenhouse gases, while animal digestion and vegetation decay contribute to methane.

options: It reduces the amount of long-wave radiation absorbed by the atmosphere.
It increases the atmosphere’s absorption of thermal radiation.
It causes sunlight to stop reaching Earth.
It prevents plants from carrying out photosynthesis.
mcqs.stem: According to the section, what happens when the concentration of greenhouse gases increases?
rationales: Incorrect: a higher concentration increases, rather than reduces, absorption of thermal radiation.
Correct: the section states that a higher concentration of greenhouse gases means greater absorption of thermal radiation.
Incorrect: incoming short-wave radiation passes through greenhouse gases to warm Earth’s surface.
Incorrect: the section does not say that greenhouse gases stop photosynthesis.

options: Sea level may rise as seawater expands and land ice melts.
Sea level must fall because oceans become colder.
All coastal areas become safer from flooding.
Rainfall stops in every region.
mcqs.stem: Which is a possible effect of global warming described in the section?
rationales: Correct: higher temperatures expand seawater, and melting ice flows into the sea, raising sea levels.
Incorrect: the section describes warming and rising sea levels, not colder oceans and falling sea levels.
Incorrect: the section warns that low-lying coastal areas may be threatened.
Incorrect: the section describes possible increases in rainfall in some regions, not a complete stop to rainfall.

options: Rice fields

mcqs.stem: Which process uses up some carbon dioxide from the air, according to the section?
rationales: Incorrect: increased farming of rice fields is listed as a cause of increased methane.
Incorrect: digestion in animals is listed as a cause of increased methane.
Incorrect: increased decay of vegetation matter is listed as a cause of increased methane.
Correct: the section says about half of the carbon dioxide is utilized by plant life during photosynthesis.

options: Winters become shorter and warmer, and summers longer and hotter.
Winters become longer and colder, and summers shorter and cooler.
Every crop grows better in higher temperatures.
Climate changes have no effect on agriculture.
mcqs.stem: What change in seasons may occur in moderate regions because of global warming?
rationales: Correct: the section says winter will be shorter and warmer and summer longer and hotter in moderate regions.
Incorrect: this is the opposite of the seasonal changes described in the section.
Incorrect: the section says some crops grow better in higher temperatures, while others do not.
Incorrect: the section states that weather changes affect the types of crops grown in different places.

written.text: Percentage of CO₂ in air is only 0.04%. Then how does it become harmful for the ecosystem?
written.finalAnswer: Although CO₂ is present in a small percentage, it absorbs outgoing thermal radiation. Increased CO₂ accumulates in the atmosphere, traps heat and raises Earth’s average temperature, causing climate changes that can harm ecosystems, agriculture and food production.

rubric.why: Recognising that a small percentage can still have an effect answers the contrast in the question.
rubric.description: Acknowledge the small percentage but explain that amount alone does not determine its effect.
rubric.how: State that even a small concentration can absorb heat.

rubric.why: The heat-absorbing property is the key cause of the greenhouse effect.
rubric.description: Explain how CO₂ affects outgoing radiation.
rubric.how: State that CO₂ absorbs some of Earth’s outgoing thermal or long-wave radiation.

rubric.why: The answer must connect heat absorption with warming.
rubric.description: Explain the result of heat being trapped.
rubric.how: Say that CO₂ accumulation slows heat loss and raises Earth’s temperature.

rubric.why: The question asks how CO₂ becomes harmful for the ecosystem.

modelAnswer: Although CO₂ makes up only 0.04% of air, it absorbs some of Earth’s outgoing thermal radiation.
The remaining CO₂ accumulates in the lower atmosphere and forms a layer that slows heat from escaping into space.
This raises Earth’s average temperature and causes global warming and climate change.
Climate change can harm ecosystems, agriculture and food production.

written.text: Why only some pollutant gases present in the atmosphere cause green house effect while others do not?
written.finalAnswer: Only gases that absorb the long-wave thermal radiation emitted by Earth contribute to the greenhouse effect. Other gases do not absorb this radiation sufficiently, so they do not trap the heat in this way.

rubric.why: The difference depends on how gases interact with Earth’s outgoing radiation.
rubric.description: Identify the relevant property of greenhouse gases.
rubric.how: State that greenhouse gases absorb outgoing long-wave or thermal radiation.

rubric.why: The answer must specify which radiation is absorbed.
rubric.description: Identify the source of the radiation.
rubric.how: Connect the radiation to Earth’s warmed surface.

rubric.why: Absorption matters because it slows heat loss to space.
rubric.how: State that the absorbed radiation is trapped or its escape to space is slowed.

rubric.why: The answer must contrast the gases that cause the effect with those that do not.
rubric.how: Explain that other gases do not absorb the outgoing radiation sufficiently to cause this effect.

modelAnswer: Earth’s surface emits long-wave thermal radiation after being warmed by the Sun.
Some pollutant gases absorb this outgoing radiation and slow its escape to space.
These gases therefore trap heat and cause the greenhouse effect.
Other gases do not absorb this radiation sufficiently, so they do not cause the greenhouse effect in this way.

written.text: Explain greenhouse effect. How is global warming dangerous for us?
written.finalAnswer: The progressive warming up of the Earth's surface due to blanketing effect of man-made carbon dioxide, methane, water vapours and other gases in the atmosphere is called Greenhouse Effect. These gases absorb some long-wave radiation emitted by Earth and slow its escape to space, raising Earth’s temperature. Global warming can raise sea levels, increase rainfall and floods, damage agriculture and food production, and make summers longer and hotter and winters shorter and warmer.

rubric.why: Absorption of outgoing radiation explains how the atmosphere warms.
rubric.how: State that greenhouse gases absorb some radiation emitted by Earth, slowing heat loss and raising temperature.

rubric.how: Mention rising sea levels, increased rainfall or floods.

rubric.why: A further consequence completes the response about dangers to people.
rubric.description: Give another danger to people or the environment.
rubric.how: Mention effects on agriculture, food production or seasonal temperatures.

modelAnswer: The progressive warming up of the Earth's surface due to blanketing effect of man-made carbon dioxide, methane, water vapours and other gases in the atmosphere is called Greenhouse Effect.
The Sun emits short-wave radiation that passes through greenhouse gases and heats Earth’s surface.
At night, Earth’s surface emits long-wave radiation, which is mostly absorbed by greenhouse gases; this slows the escape of heat to space and raises Earth’s temperature.
Global warming can expand seawater and melt ice in Antarctica and Greenland, raising sea levels and threatening low-lying coastal areas.
It can also increase rainfall and floods, affect agriculture and food production, and make summers longer and hotter and winters shorter and warmer.

examTips: The board may ask for the definition and explanation of the greenhouse effect as a descriptive question; learn the textbook definition accurately.
For a process answer, show the order: short-wave sunlight reaches Earth, Earth emits long-wave radiation, greenhouse gases absorb some of it, and Earth’s temperature rises.
Questions may ask for sources of greenhouse gases or effects of global warming. Name clear examples from the section and explain the link to warming.
For full marks on harmful effects, include more than one effect, such as rising sea levels, floods, harm to agriculture and changes in seasons.

steps.text: The progressive warming up of the Earth's surface due to blanketing effect of man-made carbon dioxide, methane, water vapours and other gases in the atmosphere is called Greenhouse Effect.

explain.title: Meaning of greenhouse effect
explain.body: The progressive warming up of the Earth's surface due to blanketing effect of man-made carbon dioxide, methane, water vapours and other gases in the atmosphere is called Greenhouse Effect.

explain.title: How heat is trapped
explain.body: Short-wave radiation from the Sun passes through greenhouse gases and heats Earth’s surface. Earth then emits long-wave radiation. Greenhouse gases absorb much of it, so Earth cools more slowly and its temperature rises.

explain.title: Why gas concentration matters
explain.body: The higher the concentration of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases, the greater the absorption of thermal radiation and the greater the increase in global warming.

explain.title: Sources and effects
explain.body: Burning coal, oil and natural gas adds greenhouse gases. Methane increases with vegetation decay, digestion in animals and increased rice farming. Global warming can raise sea levels, increase rainfall and floods, affect agriculture, and make summers longer and hotter.

mistakes: Do not confuse incoming short-wave radiation from the Sun with outgoing long-wave radiation from Earth.
Do not say greenhouse gases block all sunlight; the section says short-wave radiation passes through them.
When explaining warming, include the key link: greenhouse gases absorb outgoing radiation, slowing heat loss to space.
Do not list only one danger when a question asks how global warming is dangerous; give several effects from the section.
Do not state that all crops grow better in higher temperatures; the section says some do, while others do not.
